verdict_reason: All 12 tiles present on the sheet show one and the same subject from slightly different angles: a small urban lake ringed by narrow 4-6 storey Hanoi shophouses, with the broken tail/wing structure of a downed aircraft sticking out of the shallow water and a whitewashed tapered concrete stele on the near bank. The stele's black plaque was read at 5x on two separate photos by two different photographers and says 'DI TICH LICH SU / HO HUU TIEP va XAC MAY BAY B.52 / DA DUOC NHA NUOC CONG NHAN' with the English 'THE HISTORICAL SITE / HUU TIEP LAKE and THE WRECKAGE OF A B.52 BOMBER'. That is a single, named, unique place, so this pin is not a dumping ground. Caveat on photographer diversity: the ids fall in three tight blocks (3506431199-3506450907, 3507245310-3507257060, 8120863874), consistent with only 2-3 contributors, so the pile proves one place but not broad independent agreement. The pin itself sits about 500 m west of where Huu Tiep lake actually is (roughly 105.832,21.0367), so the coordinate is offset even though the place is real.

photos.evidence: Small lake, mirror-still, with dark twisted aircraft wreckage breaking the surface at left-centre; behind it the same row of tall narrow Hanoi houses (one with a red pyramidal turret roof) that appears in every other tile of this sheet.

Whitewashed tapered concrete stele with a dark rectangular plaque in the foreground, aircraft wreckage in the water behind it, same house row; the stele is the Huu Tiep lake / B-52 monument whose plaque text I read at 5x on other frames.
Close view across the water of the wreckage: recognisable aircraft structural spars and skin panels half-submerged, with a pale green rendered house and a blue tarpaulin stall on the far bank.
Same wreckage mass in the same shallow water, framed portrait, with the white-and-cream shophouse wall and street-level umbrella behind it.

Cropped and upscaled ~5x: the stele plaque is legible - 'DI TICH LICH SU / HO HUU TIEP va XAC MAY BAY B.52 / DA DUOC NHA NUOC CONG NHAN / THE HISTORICAL SITE / HUU TIEP LAKE and THE WRECKAGE OF A B.52 BOMBER'.
Wide view with the white stele and its plaque at right, the wreckage in the water at left, and the balconied houses ringing the pond.
Portrait view of the pond, wreckage low in the frame, the same distinctive red-turreted house and the tall white house behind.
Nearly the same framing as 3506435551 - wreckage half-submerged, pale green house and blue tarpaulin stall on the far side.
Wreckage in the water with the red-turreted house and the whole shophouse row reflected; same pond, slightly hazier light.
Visitors posing beside the base of the white stele; the stele's stone offering ledge and the pond with the house row behind identify the same spot.
Wide lake view with the wreckage at centre-left and the red-turreted and cream houses behind - the same bank as every other tile.
Cropped and upscaled ~5x: the monument plaque reads 'DI TICH LICH SU / HO HUU TIEP va XAC MAY BAY B.52 / DA DUOC NHA NUOC CONG NHAN', with the wreckage visible in the water to the left of the stele.
